questions.question: What is Windows Explorer? विंडोज एक्सप्लोरर क्या है?
questions.solution: Windows Explorer is a file management application. It allows users to navigate, view, organize, and manage files and folders on their computer. This is its primary function, distinguishing it from web browsers, antivirus programs, or media players.
The keyboard shortcut Windows key + E opens Windows Explorer. This is a standard Windows shortcut that provides quick access to the file management system without needing to navigate through menus.
The default view in Windows Explorer is Details. This view provides comprehensive information about files including name, date modified, type, and size, making it efficient for file management.
The address bar in Windows Explorer shows the Current folder location. This helps users understand their position within the file hierarchy and navigate between folders.

Quick Access displays Frequently used files and folders. This feature improves efficiency by providing easy access to commonly accessed locations without requiring users to navigate through the full folder structure.
The Navigation pane appears on the left side of Windows Explorer. This pane shows the folder hierarchy, allowing users to quickly navigate between different locations on their computer.
The extension .txt represents Text files in Windows Explorer. File extensions help the operating system identify the file type and determine which program should open it by default.

questions.solution: One can show hidden files in Windows Explorer through the View tab > Hidden items. This option toggles the visibility of hidden files and folders, which are normally concealed to prevent accidental modification.
Windows Explorer uses Multiple attributes including name, date, size, and type to sort files. This flexibility allows users to organize their files according to various criteria based on their needs.
The Details view shows the most detailed file information. This view displays columns with comprehensive information about each file, including name, date modified, type, size, and other properties.

questions.solution:
Navigation pane → Shows folder structure

o The Navigation pane is a section in file management systems (like Windows Explorer) that displays the hierarchical structure of folders and directories. It helps users navigate through different folders and drives easily.

Preview pane → Shows file contents

o The Preview pane allows users to view the contents of a selected file (e.g., text, images, or documents) without opening it. This is useful for quickly checking the content of files.

Details pane → Shows file information

o The Details pane provides metadata or information about a selected file, such as its size, type, date modified, and other properties. This helps users understand the details of a file without opening it.

Search box → Finds files and folders

o The Search box is used to search for specific files or folders within a directory or drive. By typing keywords, users can quickly locate the files or folders they need.

questions.solution: All of the above statements about file operations are correct. Files can be copied using Ctrl+C, moved using Ctrl+X, multiple files can be selected using the Ctrl key, and deleted files go to the Recycle Bin by default (unless Shift+Delete is used for permanent deletion).

questions.solution: Statements I and II only are correct about file extensions. File extensions indicate file type and can be hidden through Windows settings. However, extensions can be changed (statement III is false), though changing them might affect file functionality.

questions.solution: All of the above views are available in Windows Explorer. Large icons, List, Details, and Content views are all valid view options that can be selected based on user preference and specific needs.

· Pressing F5 in Windows Explorer refreshes the current view. This function is useful when changes have been made to files or folders by other applications or users, and you want to update the Explorer view to reflect these changes.

· Refreshing ensures that Windows Explorer displays the most current state of files and folders, including any additions, deletions, or modifications that might have occurred since the window was opened or last refreshed.
